Does it work for friends or family?
Can one bad aspect ruin a match?

Synastry is the old technique of laying one birth chart over another to see how two people meet. Your Venus touching their Mars, their Saturn sitting on your Moon: these cross contacts describe attraction, comfort and friction in a way that Sun signs alone never can. The Astrolas Synastry Chart calculates both charts, finds every contact between them and explains each one.
This guide walks through the form, the result page and a sensible reading order. If you want the background first, synastry explained covers the ideas behind it.

doan: The tool builds a birth chart for each person and draws them as a bi-wheel, one inside the other. It then lists every aspect between a planet or point in chart A and one in chart B, scores the relationship along a few themed axes, and gives you a written reading for the contacts that have one. It also offers a composite chart and a progressed comparison, which are covered below.
Planet Venus Rules Taurus, Libra Love, beauty, values
Planet Mars Rules Aries Action, energy, desire
Planet Moon Rules Cancer Emotions, intuition, nurturing

muc.ten: Step by step: filling in the form
doan: Open the Synastry Chart . The page says "Enter both birth details (or pick saved profiles) to see the synastry reading." Saved profiles appear when you are logged in; as a guest you type the data in.
For Person A and Person B (partner) the fields are the same:
Hour / Minute , or Unknown Time
City / Location , picked from the suggestions
Then choose a Relationship type :
Romantic for couples and dates;
Cooperative (siblings, friends, partners) for family, friendship or work.
The type decides which relationship rating you get, so pick the one that fits. Press View synastry .

The heading reads "Synastry Analysis". Each person gets a summary card with birth date, time and place, plus a Quick chart view menu that opens that person's own Birth chart, Solar Return, Progression, Transit, Transit + PR, Moon Phase or Zodiacal Releasing page. Below the cards you can switch Relationship type , set a Date and Current location , and press Update .
The bi-wheel comes next, labelled Person A and Person B . Display changes the theme and size, Share makes a share card, and Export copies the chart, downloads a PNG or prints a PDF.

Aspect comparison between the two natal charts. A grid with one person's planets down the side and the other's across the top, filtered by Major or Minor aspects and an Orb setting. The total count of aspects sits next to Copy .

Relationship rating. For a romantic pair you get four bars scored out of 100: Romance , Harmony & attraction , Challenges and Sexual conflict . Each bar has a label such as Moderate or Very high and lists the aspects that feed it, with orbs. The note under the bars explains the method: each cross aspect is weighted by the planet pair, the aspect type and how tight the orb is.

Aspect Interpretations. Every cross aspect with its orb, sorted tightest first, split into Harmonious and Tense counts. Contacts with a written reading get a headline and a paragraph on how the pair tends to play out. Hide secondary aspects is ticked by default and hides contacts that have no reading yet; untick it to see every aspect.
Planet tables for each person, with sign and house.
Everything described in the result screen section above lives on the Birth Charts tab and was open to guests.

Start with the tightest contacts. The top of Aspect Interpretations is sorted by orb. Anything under two degrees between personal planets (Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars) or angles is the core of the connection.
Look at the lights. Sun and Moon contacts in either direction speak to basic comfort. The Sun and Moon compatibility cheat sheet is a quick guide.
Then Venus and Mars. These describe affection, desire and how each of you acts on it. Venus sign and Mars sign gives the background.
Check the angles. Planets on the other person's Ascendant or Descendant are felt at once. See the rising sign explained .

Read the bars last. The ratings summarise the list you have just read. A high Challenges score next to a high Harmony score is common in lasting relationships; tension is not the same as incompatibility.
Aspect names on their own mean little until you know the families, so keep aspects explained close. For the relationship as its own entity, the composite chart explained is the next step.
Run it twice, once as Romantic and once as Cooperative, if the relationship is not clearly one or the other. The bars change; the aspects do not.
Read contacts in both directions. Your Moon on their Saturn feels different from their Moon on your Saturn, and the reading says who is doing what.
Outer planet contacts between people of a similar age (Uranus to Neptune, Pluto to Pluto) are shared by a whole generation, and the readings say so. Give them less weight.
Save the page URL. It holds both sets of birth data, so you can come back without typing anything. How to save and compare charts has more.
The compatibility checker gives one quick score from birth dates. Synastry uses full birth data, draws the bi-wheel, rates several axes and explains each contact.
Yes. Choose Cooperative (siblings, friends, partners) as the relationship type.
No. Every real pair has hard contacts. Look at the balance and at how the tight aspects fit together, not at any single line.
Enter both sets of birth data, choose the relationship type and begin with the tightest aspects at the top of the list. You can open the tool directly at /synastry-chart .
